First issue: The third miner in the photo won't hash, I believe due to a power-related issue. I tried it on several outlets and the same message came up. Another photo of the screen on the third miner is attached. Second potential issue: The first miner from the first photo is hashing properly but every now and then it goes offline, reboots and comes back online. What's the recourse? Kindly, Tom C.: Here's the second photo showing the power-related issue.
You: Sorry, Tom. Most likely on both is the power supply not holding under load, the one that won't hash and the one that reboots. Was either unit overclocked, and what wattage brick is each on? For the dead one, start the RMA now and we'll send a label: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12t6skK21Qb8GfAdUQ9nOhJ1tVINJ60T3AIAsyhBwnYM/viewform PSU-only replacements exist, so the whole unit may not need to go back. Hal (HeliumDeploy): Hi Tom, Hal here, I am the technical side of the HeliumDeploy team. I opened both photos and went through them properly. What I can see: 1. Middle unit: healthy. 5968.6 GH/s, 104.25 W, 50 °C, core at 1148 mV drawing 4953 mA. That is exactly where a NerdQaxe++ Rev 5.1 Pro should sit. 2. Third unit (close-up): it boots, joins Wi-Fi at 192.168.1.158, and it has hashed before (best difficulty 55.9M). Then the screen shows CURRENT PROTECTION, Guru Meditation #51A00000, 0.0 GH/s, 0.062 W, 35 °C. In plain terms, the voltage regulator's overcurrent protection has tripped and cut power to the ASICs.
